definition: Lexical Variant Generation (LVG) is a suite of command-line interface (CLI) tools designed to perform lexical transformations on text.
details: The primary goal is to generate lexical variants for Natural language processing of patient clinical documents.

explainer.lead: LVG is a suite of command-line tools that produce lexical variants of words. It matters in clinical text processing, where the same medical concept appears in many surface forms across patient documents.

tiers.eli5: It takes a word and lists the other forms it might show up as, so a computer can spot them all as the same thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run LVG over clinical notes to normalise inflected and alternate word forms before downstream matching or indexing. A pitfall is over-expanding variants and creating false matches between distinct terms.
tiers.paperLevel: A CLI tool suite performing lexical transformations on input text; it defines no formal guarantees about variant completeness or correctness.

explainer.example: Given a clinical term in a patient note, LVG outputs its lexical transformations so a downstream system can match the alternate forms.
